title: IPS at OCC:
title_q: “You Haven't Been Introduced to Us Yet”
headline: Men in an Omaha prison speak to the public: you only know our number and our past. Meet us.
story: One question from MHA staff to a peer support circle at OCC: what do you wish the public knew about IPS? The men answer one at a time. They do this because they want to, not because they have to. They are not there to fix anyone, only to support. “What you know about us is a number and what we did in the past.”
This is the men's own voice. No names on screen. Dignified and hopeful: it ends on a man asking people to reach out and say, are you okay? It must not repeat the Lincoln prison video.
do: Open on frame 1 on the older man with glasses, already talking, with the hook text.
One line = one man. Never join two men into one sentence.
Stay on the speaker. Cut away only when a shot shows what he says.
Lift the faces gently. The room is dim.
End on the hug (C4893) under “are you okay?”.
dont: No names, no prison numbers, no crimes on screen. No name supers.
Do not zoom in on an ID badge or name tag. Blur any that is readable.
Not the Lincoln video: no cards, no chess, no use-of-force, not its hook text.
No “inmate”, “offender”, “patient”, “treatment” or “therapy” in any text you write.
No dark music, no slow motion, no bars or fences as a symbol.
